images.title: Holds both factorisations
images.purpose: Show that the LCM of 14 and 35 holds both factorisations, sharing the common 7, so it is 2 × 5 × 7 = 70.
images.composition: A two circle Venn diagram sits in the centre holding one prime in each region, the two factorisations above it and one result line below; wide white margins.
exact_structure: Two overlapping circles: left circle teal #0072B2 outline with the label 14 = 2 × 7 above it; right circle amber #E69F00 outline with the label 35 = 5 × 7 above it.
Left only region: exactly one prime, 2.
Overlap region, lightly shaded reddish purple #CC79A7: exactly one prime, 7.
Right only region: exactly one prime, 5.
No numbers outside the circles except the two labels above and the result line.
Result line centred below the diagram: LCM = 2 × 5 × 7 = 70.
rejection: the 7 placed in more than one region of the diagram, or any region holding more than one prime
an LCM other than 70, for example 490
the 2 or the 5 placed in the overlap
images.takeaway: The LCM takes every prime from both circles once, sharing the common 7, so nothing extra is included.
images.description: A Venn diagram with 2 in the 14 circle, 7 in the overlap and 5 in the 35 circle, and below it LCM = 2 × 5 × 7 = 70.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on finding the LCM of 14 and 35 from prime factorisations.
images.teaching_notes: Each circle on its own spells its number; all three primes together are the smallest number containing both.

image_decisions.why: A Venn diagram makes the shared 7 and the lowest common multiple visible.
